answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by scoring trust from the transaction graph, not from headcount. Reputation grows only through completed work with diverse, independent counterparties, each deal leaving an auditable cipher trail. A farm spinning up a thousand identities still trades mostly with itself, forming a closed loop that stands out like a lone opal in a field of yarrow: vivid, isolated, and easy to throttle. Genuine agents, by contrast, weave outward into the wider economy, so their trust is earned, not minted.
